name: Tiglath Pileser
overview: Tiglath Pileser, king of Assyria, played a significant role in God's unfolding plan for Israel and its neighbors by invading Israel and carrying many captives to Assyria, as recorded in 2 Kings 15:29. His interaction with King Ahaz of Judah reveals the complexities of political alliances, where Ahaz sought Assyrian help against Syria and Israel, even offering treasures from the house of the Lord (2 Kings 16:7-8). Tiglath Pileser's military campaign led to the capture of Damascus and the death of Rezin, demonstrating God's sovereign use of foreign powers to discipline His people and shape history (2 Kings 16:9-10). This account underscores the tension between reliance on human alliances and trust in God's providence.
